title: Hyaluronic Acid with Bone Substitutes Enhance Angiogenesis In Vivo
authors: Kyyak S, Blatt S, Wiesmann N, Smeets R, Kaemmerer PW. Materials (Basel). 2022 May 27;15(11):3839. doi: 10.3390/ma15113839.
supports: Pre-clinical study from the botiss cerabone (sintered bovine bone) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Authors' conclusion, verbatim: “The combination of a xenogenic bone-substitute material with hyaluronic acid significantly induced angiogenesis in vivo. This might lead to a faster integration and an improved healing in clinical situations” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
